decisions.reason: The encrypted second channel remains core to the announced vision of binding mobile communication and one secure identity, so management will keep it even though it is no longer visible on the website, likely because it was folded into the platform offering.

Mobile PDF signing underpins the publicly stated push into online contract signing, and the pandemic-driven demand for remote signatures lets management attribute weak earlier results to temporary market immaturity.
The multi-layer end-to-end security architecture is the backbone of the integrated offer and embodies heavy R&D investment, so dropping it would undermine the firm's whole positioning.

Despite the market shift to app-based authentication and its absence from the website, the sunk hardware investment and remaining regulated customers lead management to keep supporting the token rather than admit failure.
The payment security compliance suite supports the regulatory positioning the firm has publicly committed to, and slow uptake can still be blamed on lengthy compliance adoption cycles.
